In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the chordoma cells are derived from the notochordal cells and express the proteins characteristic of both embryonal and differentiatinal tissues.

the embryonal proteins CEA and cytokingen are expressed in the primary and metastatic chordomas but not in the normal notochords, whereas the differentiational protein S-100 is expressed in the normal notochonds and in the primary and the metastatic chordomas.

the expression of S-100 is a constant feature of the chordoma cells, whereas the expression of CEA and cytotoxins is variable and is influenced by the environment of the cells in which they are found.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the chordoma may be regarded as a neoplasm with an immature phenotype.
the embryonal proteins are expressed in the primary chordomas, but the differentiational ones in the metastatic chordomas.
the expression of the embryonic and differentiational markers in chordomas is not a constant phenomenon, but is variable and depends on the microenvironment in each case.
The main takeaway from our work is that
chordomas are a group of tumors that are very similar to each other and that they can express a variety of different proteins.
the S-100 protein, CEA, and cytokeratin are expressed in some cases, but not all cases, of chordomas.
S-100 is a useful diagnostic marker of chordomas, and that CEA and cytotoxin may be useful markers for predicting the prognosis of chordoma patients.
